IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. OF 2024  (arising out of SLP(Crl.) No. 910/2024)
 ABHISHEK   VERSUS  STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH & ANR. ..... RESP
O R D E R Leave granted.
The identity of respondent No. 2, who is the informant/ complainant will be suppressed.
Her name will be deleted from the case file, paper books and other relevant papers.
The original memo of parties containing the name/details of respondent No. 2, will be kept in a sealed cover.
In this matter, we had issued notice, vide order dated 25.01.2024.
Thereafter, the matter was adjourned to ensure that the evidence of the informant/complainant was recorded in Court.
Several allegations have been made by the parties inter se, though it is accepted that parties knew each other before their marriage.
The complaint/Crime/First Information Report1 dated 30.09.2022, including the occurrence in question, was post the filing of the divorce petition.
for nearly one year.
Certain allegations have been made with regard 1 FIR, for short to the electronic files/e-files, which have been disputed by the appellant, Abhishek.
The appellant has also relied upon the conversation he had had with the close family members of the informant/complainant.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, including the period of incarceration suffered of nearly one year, we accept the present appeal and direct that the appellant, Abhishek,
will be released on bail during pendency of the trial in the chargesheet arising out of Crime/FIR No.
449/2022 dated 30.09.2022 registered with police station  M.G. Road, District Indore, Madhya Pradesh, for offence(s) punishable under Sections 377, 498A, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16484797/
1 1860 and Sections 66E and 67A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, on terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial Court, which may include the terms mentioned in sub-Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
In addition, the appellant, Abhishek, will submit his passport in the trial Court and will not leave India without the permission of the trial Court.

The appellant, Abhishek, will not get in touch with the informant/complainant or any of her family members on phone/social media or physically.
He shall not upload any photograph of the informant/complainant, either alone or with him, on the social media/application or otherwise share the same with any third person.
In case there is any violation of the aforesaid terms and conditions, the trial Court will be at liberty to cancel the bail.
The impugned judgment is set aside and the appeal is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
We clarify that the observations made in this order are for grant of bail and disposal of the present appeal and the same will not be treated as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
The trial will proceed in accordance with law and the case shall be decided on the basis of evidence and material led.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
..................J. (SANJIV KHANNA) ..................J. (SANJAY KUMAR) NEW DELHI;
OCTOBER 01, 2024.

D.A.G. Mr. Ramesh Thakur, Adv.

Mr. Pashupathi Nath Razdan, AOR Mr. Sunil Kumar Singh, Adv.
Ms. Mukti Singh, AOR UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following O R D E R Leave granted.
The identity of respondent No. 2, who is the informant/ complainant will be suppressed.
Her name will be deleted from the case file, paper books and other relevant papers.
The original memo of parties containing the name/details of respondent No. 2, will be kept in a sealed cover.
I.A. no. 97722/2024 is accordingly allowed.

In terms of the signed order, the present appeal is accepted and it is directed that the appellant, Abhishek, will be released on bail during pendency of the trial in the chargesheet arising out of Crime/FIR No.
449/2022 dated 30.09.2022 registered with police station  M.G. Road, District Indore, Madhya Pradesh, for offence(s) punishable under Sections 377, 498A, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 66E and 67A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, on terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial Court, which may include the terms mentioned in sub-Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
In addition, the appellant, Abhishek, will submit his passport in the trial Court and will not leave India without the permission of the trial Court.
He shall provide the mobile number, on which he can be contacted by the Investigating Officer while he is on bail to ascertain his whereabouts.
The appellant, Abhishek, will not get in touch with the informant/complainant or any of her family members on phone/social media or physically.
He shall not upload any photograph of the informant/complainant, either alone or with him, on the social media/application or otherwise share the same with any third person.
The appeal is allowed in the terms of the signed order.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

(DEEPAK GUGLANI) (R.S. NARAYANAN)
